correctness.rationale: The 2n+1 closed-neighborhood rule makes a vertex flip iff >=n of its 2n neighbors agree with it, exactly the non-decreasing-cut condition. The cut functional 2n(x+y+z)-2(xy+xz+yz) is multi-affine; its maximizers are precisely states with two monochromatic opposite parts and the third free. A sweep makes A unanimous and B opposite in <=2n permitted flips, yielding a path from any state. The six n-cubes intersect in six nonconstant monochromatic junctions, giving 6(2^n-1) recurrent states; all neutral flips are reversible, making uniform pi stationary. Two endpoints yield precisely 2n outgoing directed flips from a chosen face; Q/pi(F)=2/(3*2^n). The TV bound via pi(.|F) and a crossing union bound gives t_mix(1/4)>floor(3*2^n/4); n=2 stationary face mass bound also holds. Hypercube edge count gives local activity 2^n/[3(2^n-1)]. Independent maxcut enumeration confirms recurrent candidate size 18,42,90 for n=2,3,4. A finite check is not the all-n proof.
